Our bank flagged invoice INV-4392 (due 2026-07-05) for a VAT ID mismatch on Redwood's invoice and placed the payment on hold. Our AP team needs either a corrected invoice or confirmation that the supply is reverse-charge eligible so we can release payment.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood intends to apply reverse-charge on this invoice, or
- Provide a corrected invoice showing Lumenware's VAT ID and the reverse-charge note, or
- If you need a VAT certificate from us, I can attach it.

We'd like to resolve this today — the PO (PO-77821) is against a time-sensitive integration project.

Thanks,

Hi Sophie — thanks for the heads up.

We're on it. Quick summary of what we need/do from our side: 
- Can you attach your VAT certificate (VAT ID proof) to this thread? That will speed verification.
- I'll engage Sales (Ben) to confirm the contract treatment (reverse-charge vs self-bill) and provide a suggested invoice split if needed.

I've CC'd Ben so he can confirm the contractual intent — if Redwood is to treat this as a reverse-charge B2B supply to Lumenware (EU), we can reissue with the appropriate note and your VAT ID. If there's any ambiguity we may ask for the scanned certificate (signed).

I'll circulate the proposed invoice layout by EOD. If you can attach the VAT cert now that would be ideal.

On Tue, Jul 7, 2026 at 10:05 Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> We're on it. Quick summary of what we need/do from our side:
> - Can you attach your VAT certificate (VAT ID proof) to this thread? That will speed verification.

Thanks, Irene — confirming Redwood's position: the contract for PO-77821 covers hosted API usage (platform access) which is ordinarily a B2B service eligible for reverse-charge where the buyer is VAT-registered in the EU.

Plan I'd propose:
1) We validate the VAT ID via VIES once Sophie uploads the certificate.
2) If validated, Accounting will reissue INV-4392 with the reverse-charge statement and Lumenware's VAT ID; the invoice will show a zero VAT line and a note: 'Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted by the customer'.
3) Alternatively, if AP requires, we can issue a split invoice that isolates platform fees (reverse-charge) and any local taxable services. I've attached a draft split (proposed_invoice_split.xlsx) showing how we would break line items and preserve revenue recognition for Redwood.

If Lumenware can sign a short payment release form (legal) confirming they're the liable VAT party, we can ask our bank to allow payment to proceed pending the correction. I've attached a template payment_release_form.pdf — legal can tweak if needed.

Ben
Sr. Accounts Lead | Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie — received, thank you. Quick update and action items so we can close this today: 

1) Validation: I validated the VAT ID you attached against VIES (EU VAT check). Link: https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/services/checkVatService. Status: valid (validation reference: VIES-20260709-9921).

2) Invoice action: Accounting will reissue INV-4392 as INV-4392-RC with the reverse-charge statement and Lumenware's VAT ID on it. The reissued invoice will be sent within 2 business hours.

3) Partial payment: To allow your AP to release funds while we reissue, please review and sign the payment_release_form.pdf (we've created a DocuSign envelope). DocuSign link: https://docusign.net/signer/ABCD1234. Once signed, we will notify the bank and request release of the held funds.

4) Collections handoff: CC'ed Ava from Collections to confirm when payment posts and to reconcile once the reissued invoice is in the system.

Attachments sent to you (from our side): proposed_invoice_split.xlsx (for future reference), payment_release_form.pdf (please sign).

If anything changes, call me on my mobile. Appreciate the quick turnaround — we'll mark this resolved in our ledger after payment clears.

Best,
